1.question: Which measure of centre is most affected by outliers?
options: Median
Mode
Mean
Interquartile range
1.explanation: Extreme values pull the mean toward them.

1.question: Supervised learning requires:
options: Unlabelled data
Labelled training data
No data
Only images

1.question: k-means is an example of:
options: Classification
Clustering
Regression
Reinforcement learning
1.explanation: k-means groups unlabelled points into k clusters.

1.question: Overfitting means a model:
options: Performs well on new data
Memorises the training data and generalises poorly
Is too simple
Has no parameters
1.correctAnswer: Memorises the training data and generalises poorly
1.explanation: It fits noise in the training set.

1.question: Which chart best shows the distribution of one numeric variable?
options: Pie chart
Histogram
Line chart
Gantt chart
1.explanation: Histograms bin values to show their distribution.

1.question: Precision is defined as:
options: TP / (TP + FN)
TP / (TP + FP)
TN / (TN + FP)
(TP + TN) / total
1.explanation: Of all predicted positives, the share that were correct.

1.question: Which algorithm predicts a continuous value?
options: Logistic regression
Linear regression
Decision tree classifier
k-means
1.explanation: Linear regression outputs a real number.

1.question: A correlation coefficient of −1 means:
options: No relationship
A perfect negative linear relationship
A perfect positive relationship
Random noise
1.explanation: As one variable rises, the other falls exactly linearly.

1.question: Which split is commonly used to evaluate a model?
options: Train / test
Read / write
Input / output
Front / back
1.explanation: Hold out test data the model never saw during training.

1.question: Association rule mining is commonly used for:
options: Market basket analysis
Image compression
Packet routing
Password hashing
1.explanation: It finds items frequently bought together, e.g. {bread} → {butter}.

2.question: What is Cross-validation?
options: Training once on every row and reporting accuracy on those same rows.
Sorting records by the label before taking a single cut.
Rotating which fold is tested so each record is used for testing in exactly one round.
Deleting every column that contains any missing value.
2.correctAnswer: Rotating which fold is tested so each record is used for testing in exactly one round.
2.explanation: Each fold takes a turn as the test set, so every record is tested once and trained on the rest.

2.question: What is Precision?
options: The fraction of actual positives that the model successfully finds.
The fraction of positive predictions that are actually positive.
The fraction of all records that receive the correct label.
The average distance from points to their assigned center.
2.correctAnswer: The fraction of positive predictions that are actually positive.
2.explanation: Precision looks only at the predicted-positive set and asks how many of those predictions are right.

2.question: What is Recall?
options: The fraction of predicted positives that truly are positive.
The share of itemsets whose confidence exceeds 1.
The fraction of actual positive records that the model correctly labels positive.
The number of centers that moved on the last k-means step.
2.correctAnswer: The fraction of actual positive records that the model correctly labels positive.
2.explanation: Recall uses the actual positives as the denominator and counts how many of them were caught.

2.question: What is F1 score?
options: The ratio of attributes kept to attributes discarded.
The arithmetic mean of training accuracy and test accuracy.
The harmonic mean of precision and recall.
The product of support and confidence for one rule.
2.correctAnswer: The harmonic mean of precision and recall.
2.explanation: The harmonic mean stays high only when both precision and recall are high, so neither error is ignored.

2.question: What is Support?
options: Among transactions with the antecedent, the fraction that also contain the consequent.
The depth of the deepest leaf in a classification tree.
The fraction of all transactions that contain a given itemset.
The distance between two cluster centers.
2.correctAnswer: The fraction of all transactions that contain a given itemset.
2.explanation: Support counts how often the itemset itself appears, divided by the number of transactions.

2.question: What is Confidence?
options: The portion of variance captured by the first principal component.
The prior probability of the majority class in the whole training file.
Among transactions that contain the antecedent, the fraction that also contain the consequent.
The fraction of all transactions that contain both the antecedent and the consequent.
2.correctAnswer: Among transactions that contain the antecedent, the fraction that also contain the consequent.
2.explanation: Confidence is a conditional share: it restricts attention to baskets that already contain the antecedent.

2.question: What is Lift?
options: The number of folds used when every record is tested once.
The raw count of transactions that contain an itemset.
How many times more often the consequent occurs with the antecedent than it occurs by chance.
The margin width of a separating hyperplane.
2.correctAnswer: How many times more often the consequent occurs with the antecedent than it occurs by chance.
2.explanation: Lift divides the rule's confidence by the consequent's overall frequency, so 1 means no association beyond chance.

2.question: What is Entropy?
options: The Euclidean distance from a point to the origin.
The percentage of association rules removed after mining.
The count of blank cells in a single column.
A class-impurity measure that is zero for a pure node and largest when class shares are equal.
2.correctAnswer: A class-impurity measure that is zero for a pure node and largest when class shares are equal.
2.explanation: Entropy uses class proportions and reaches zero only when one class occupies the whole node.

2.question: What is Information gain?
options: The drop in entropy achieved by splitting a set of records on one chosen attribute.
The support of the single most frequent item.
The increase in cluster radius after one more point joins the cluster.
The ratio of test accuracy to training accuracy.
2.correctAnswer: The drop in entropy achieved by splitting a set of records on one chosen attribute.
2.explanation: Gain subtracts the weighted child entropy from the parent entropy, so a useful split yields a positive drop.

2.question: What is Naive Bayes?
options: A clusterer that merges the two closest groups at every step.
A classifier that multiplies the class prior by feature likelihoods while assuming features are independent given the class.
A tree that chooses every split by Gini impurity alone.
A miner that ranks rules by lift and ignores class labels.
2.correctAnswer: A classifier that multiplies the class prior by feature likelihoods while assuming features are independent given the class.
2.explanation: Bayes' rule supplies the class probability, and the naive step factors the joint likelihood into per-feature terms.

3.question: What is Support vector machine?
options: A bar chart of predicted probabilities on the training rows only.
A classifier that separates classes using the decision boundary with the widest margin.
An algorithm that grows a cluster outward from a dense core point.
A method that replaces missing numbers with the column median.
3.correctAnswer: A classifier that separates classes using the decision boundary with the widest margin.
3.explanation: The optimal boundary maximizes the gap to the nearest points of each class, which are the support vectors.

3.question: What is k-nearest neighbors?
options: A tree whose weak branches are removed after a validation check.
A score equal to the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
A method that maintains k centers and moves each center to its cluster mean.
A classifier that labels a new point by the majority class of its k closest training points.
3.correctAnswer: A classifier that labels a new point by the majority class of its k closest training points.
3.explanation: The prediction is a vote of nearby labeled points, and no explicit boundary is stored during training.

3.question: What is Hierarchical clustering?
options: Predicting a numeric bill with a straight-line equation.
Building a nested tree of clusters by repeatedly merging or splitting groups according to a linkage distance.
Assigning every point to one of k fixed centers and updating those centers.
Replacing category names with integers that pretend to have order.
3.correctAnswer: Building a nested tree of clusters by repeatedly merging or splitting groups according to a linkage distance.
3.explanation: Each merge or split is kept, so the result is a hierarchy rather than one flat partition.

3.question: What is DBSCAN?
options: A table used only to derive precision and recall.
A density-based clusterer that grows clusters from core points and marks sparse points as noise.
A method that requires the user to choose k and represents each cluster by its mean.
A supervised model that outputs class probabilities from a prior and likelihoods.
3.correctAnswer: A density-based clusterer that grows clusters from core points and marks sparse points as noise.
3.explanation: Membership follows density reachability from core points, so arbitrary shapes and noise points are allowed.

3.question: What is Silhouette coefficient?
options: The count of attributes remaining after selection.
The fraction of test records that received the correct class label.
A score from -1 to 1 that is high when a point is much closer to its own cluster than to the next cluster.
The minimum support required to keep an itemset.
3.correctAnswer: A score from -1 to 1 that is high when a point is much closer to its own cluster than to the next cluster.
3.explanation: The score compares a point's average distance inside its cluster with its average distance to the nearest other cluster.

3.question: What is Training set?
options: The unlabeled batch scored after the model is deployed.
The labeled records used to fit a model's parameters or structure.
The records held aside solely to estimate final performance.
The list of attributes removed as irrelevant.
3.correctAnswer: The labeled records used to fit a model's parameters or structure.
3.explanation: Fitting uses these records to set splits, weights, or probabilities before any final test.

3.question: What is Test set?
options: The centers produced by the first k-means iteration.
Labeled records withheld from training and used to estimate performance on new data.
The records whose errors are used to update the model during fitting.
The product list used to count how often an item is bought.
3.correctAnswer: Labeled records withheld from training and used to estimate performance on new data.
3.explanation: Because the model never fit these labels, their errors estimate generalization.

3.question: What is Holdout method?
options: A bootstrap sample drawn with replacement to train each tree in a forest.
Several rotated splits in which every record is tested exactly once.
A single split of labeled data into a training portion and a separate test portion.
A projection of all columns onto two variance-maximizing axes.
3.correctAnswer: A single split of labeled data into a training portion and a separate test portion.
3.explanation: Holdout performs one partition into train and test rather than rotating several folds.

3.question: What is Min-max normalization?
options: Scaling a numeric attribute into a fixed range, often 0 to 1, using its minimum and maximum.
Replacing each category with several orthogonal binary columns.
Subtracting the mean and dividing by the standard deviation.
Cutting a continuous attribute into equal-width bins.
3.correctAnswer: Scaling a numeric attribute into a fixed range, often 0 to 1, using its minimum and maximum.
3.explanation: The minimum maps to the low end of the range and the maximum maps to the high end, with values scaled linearly between them.

3.question: What is Z-score standardization?
options: Rescaling a numeric attribute so that its mean is 0 and its standard deviation is 1.
Replacing extreme points with the nearest boxplot whisker.
Mapping every value linearly onto 0 to 1 using the minimum and maximum.
Splitting a date into separate year, month, and day columns.
3.correctAnswer: Rescaling a numeric attribute so that its mean is 0 and its standard deviation is 1.
3.explanation: Subtracting the mean centers the column at 0, and dividing by the standard deviation sets the spread to 1.

4.question: What is Missing value imputation?
options: Sorting the file so blank cells fall at the bottom and then ignoring them in reports only.
Assigning a random class label to rows that already have labels.
Filling absent entries with estimated values such as a mean, median, mode, or model prediction.
Deleting every column that stores any numeric measurement.
4.correctAnswer: Filling absent entries with estimated values such as a mean, median, mode, or model prediction.
4.explanation: Imputation puts a substitute value into an empty cell so the row can remain in the analysis.

4.question: What is Outlier?
options: An item that appears in every transaction in the log.
A record whose values lie unusually far from the bulk of the data and may distort a model.
The most frequent class in a labeled training set.
A leaf that contains exactly one training record of the majority class.
4.correctAnswer: A record whose values lie unusually far from the bulk of the data and may distort a model.
4.explanation: The record is extreme relative to the rest of the sample, so means, distances, or splits can be pulled toward it.

4.question: What is Discretization?
options: Converting a continuous attribute into a small number of ordered bins or intervals.
Scaling a column to mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
Dropping attributes whose correlation with the label is high.
Expanding one category into several binary indicator columns.
4.correctAnswer: Converting a continuous attribute into a small number of ordered bins or intervals.
4.explanation: Each numeric value is replaced by the interval that contains it, so the attribute becomes categorical and ordered.

4.question: What is One-hot encoding?
options: Replacing each category by an integer rank from 1 through the number of levels.
Splitting a numeric column at its median into two bins.
Hashing every text field into one shared numeric identifier.
Representing a categorical attribute as binary columns, one per category, with a single 1 in the active column.
4.correctAnswer: Representing a categorical attribute as binary columns, one per category, with a single 1 in the active column.
4.explanation: Each category gets its own column, so the coding does not invent a false numeric order among categories.

4.question: What is Dimensionality reduction?
options: Copying minority-class rows until the class counts match.
Adding an interaction column for every pair of original attributes.
Growing a tree until every training leaf is pure.
Representing records with fewer attributes while keeping as much useful structure as possible.
4.correctAnswer: Representing records with fewer attributes while keeping as much useful structure as possible.
4.explanation: The transformed records use fewer coordinates, but the kept coordinates are chosen to preserve variation or class structure.

4.question: What is Principal component analysis?
options: A clustering step that sets k equal to the number of known classes.
A supervised ranking of attributes by chi-square association with the class label.
A filter that keeps only association rules whose lift is above 1.
An unsupervised transform that builds uncorrelated axes ordered by how much variance they capture.
4.correctAnswer: An unsupervised transform that builds uncorrelated axes ordered by how much variance they capture.
4.explanation: Each next component is orthogonal to the earlier ones and captures as much remaining variance as possible.

4.question: What is Underfitting?
options: Memorizing training quirks so that new records are predicted poorly.
Building a tree whose every leaf contains only one class.
Obtaining a clustering whose silhouette scores are close to 1.
Using a model too weak to capture the real pattern, so error stays high on both training and new data.
4.correctAnswer: Using a model too weak to capture the real pattern, so error stays high on both training and new data.
4.explanation: The model class cannot represent the signal, so even the training error remains large.

4.question: What is Bias-variance tradeoff?
options: The choice between Euclidean distance and Manhattan distance.
The balance between a model's systematic error and its sensitivity to the particular training sample.
The choice between precision and recall when the positive class is rare.
The gap between support and confidence of one association rule.
4.correctAnswer: The balance between a model's systematic error and its sensitivity to the particular training sample.
4.explanation: Simpler models tend to have higher bias and lower variance, while more flexible models do the reverse.

4.question: What is ROC curve?
options: A plot of true-positive rate against false-positive rate as the decision threshold changes.
A plot of training loss against the number of passes through the training file.
A bar chart of how many records belong to each class in the raw file.
A tree diagram of merge distances from hierarchical clustering.
4.correctAnswer: A plot of true-positive rate against false-positive rate as the decision threshold changes.
4.explanation: Each threshold gives one true-positive rate and one false-positive rate, and those pairs trace the curve.

4.question: What is AUC?
options: The number of true negatives in one confusion matrix.
The accuracy obtained at one chosen probability cutoff.
The area under the ROC curve, summarizing ranking quality across all decision thresholds.
The height of the tallest bar in a class-count histogram.
4.correctAnswer: The area under the ROC curve, summarizing ranking quality across all decision thresholds.
4.explanation: Integrating the ROC curve rewards a model that ranks positives above negatives across thresholds, not at one cutoff.

5.question: What is True positive?
options: An actual positive record that the classifier predicts as negative.
An actual negative record that the classifier predicts as negative.
An actual negative record that the classifier predicts as positive.
An actual positive record that the classifier also predicts as positive.
5.correctAnswer: An actual positive record that the classifier also predicts as positive.
5.explanation: Both the true label and the predicted label are positive, so the prediction is a hit on a positive case.

5.question: What is Supervised learning?
options: Learning a mapping from inputs to a known target by using examples that already include that target.
Searching for groups in records that were collected without a target label.
Discovering which products are bought together without using a class label.
Compressing attributes into fewer coordinates without predicting an output.
5.correctAnswer: Learning a mapping from inputs to a known target by using examples that already include that target.
5.explanation: The training examples include the target, so the learner can compare predictions with known answers.

5.question: What is Unsupervised learning?
options: Estimating accuracy with a labeled holdout set.
Choosing the attribute split that most reduces class entropy.
Finding structure such as clusters or dense regions when no target label is given.
Fitting a classifier on examples whose class label is already known.
5.correctAnswer: Finding structure such as clusters or dense regions when no target label is given.
5.explanation: Without a target, the algorithm can only use similarities or densities among the inputs.

5.question: What is Apriori algorithm?
options: A kernel method that maximizes the margin between two classes.
A frequent-itemset method that extends a set only when every one of its subsets is already frequent.
A split rule that always chooses the attribute with the lowest Gini impurity.
A clustering loop that replaces each center with the mean of its assigned points.
5.correctAnswer: A frequent-itemset method that extends a set only when every one of its subsets is already frequent.
5.explanation: If a subset is infrequent, every larger set containing it is infrequent, so those candidates are pruned.

5.question: What is Gini impurity?
options: The silhouette of one point's cluster assignment.
The fraction of transactions that contain a chosen itemset.
The width of the margin around a separating hyperplane.
A split score that is zero for a pure node and higher when class proportions are more evenly mixed.
5.correctAnswer: A split score that is zero for a pure node and higher when class proportions are more evenly mixed.
5.explanation: Gini impurity is computed from class proportions and vanishes only when a single class fills the node.

5.question: What is Pruning?
options: Adding attributes until every training leaf contains only one class.
Removing branches from a grown tree so the tree overfits less and predicts new records better.
Increasing k until every point is its own cluster.
Lowering minimum support until nearly every itemset is kept.
5.correctAnswer: Removing branches from a grown tree so the tree overfits less and predicts new records better.
5.explanation: Branches that fit training noise are cut, which usually lowers error on data the tree did not fit.

5.question: What is Ensemble method?
options: Replacing the model with a prediction of the majority class for every row.
Keeping only the single attribute with the highest correlation to the label.
Stopping when training accuracy first reaches 100 percent.
Combining several models so their joint prediction is more stable than any one of the models.
5.correctAnswer: Combining several models so their joint prediction is more stable than any one of the models.
5.explanation: Errors that differ across members can cancel when the members vote or average their predictions.

5.question: What is Random forest?
options: A density clusterer that requires a neighborhood radius and a core-point count.
An ensemble of decision trees, each trained on a bootstrap sample and a random subset of attributes at each split.
One unpruned tree that tests every attribute in order at the root.
A Bayes classifier that assumes features are independent given the class.
5.correctAnswer: An ensemble of decision trees, each trained on a bootstrap sample and a random subset of attributes at each split.
5.explanation: Bootstrap samples and random attribute subsets make the trees differ, and their votes form the forest prediction.

5.question: What is Market basket analysis?
options: Grouping stores by floor area and number of employees.
Mining retail transactions to find items that customers tend to purchase together.
Labeling product reviews as positive or negative sentiment.
Forecasting tomorrow's total store revenue from a daily sales time series.
5.correctAnswer: Mining retail transactions to find items that customers tend to purchase together.
5.explanation: Each transaction is a basket, and the analysis looks for co-occurring items rather than a class label.

5.question: What is Data cleaning?
options: Drawing an ROC curve after the classifier has already been trained.
Scoring a deployed model on live traffic that has no labels yet.
Detecting and repairing errors, duplicates, and inconsistent codes in records before analysis.
Choosing k from the elbow of a within-cluster distance plot.
5.correctAnswer: Detecting and repairing errors, duplicates, and inconsistent codes in records before analysis.
5.explanation: Cleaning fixes what is wrong or duplicated in the records themselves, before transforms or models run.

6.question: Which situation illustrates Data preprocessing?
options: A grocer learns that baskets containing diapers also often contain baby wipes.
A mailbox assigns each incoming message to spam or not spam using messages labeled last year.
A clinic rescales lab units and fills blank glucose cells before training a readmission model.
An online shop groups visitors by pages viewed without using any predefined segment names.
6.correctAnswer: A clinic rescales lab units and fills blank glucose cells before training a readmission model.
6.explanation: Models expect consistent, usable fields, so cleaning and transforming records is the preparation step before mining.

6.question: Which situation illustrates Classification?
options: An online shop groups visitors by pages viewed without using any predefined segment names.
A credit model asks about income, then about missed payments, and a leaf predicts default or not.
A mailbox assigns each incoming message to spam or not spam using messages labeled last year.
A grocer learns that baskets containing diapers also often contain baby wipes.
6.correctAnswer: A mailbox assigns each incoming message to spam or not spam using messages labeled last year.
6.explanation: The target is a known class, and the model learns that class from labeled examples.

6.question: Which situation illustrates Clustering?
options: A carrier splits 20000 subscribers into 4 groups by minutes, data use, and monthly bill.
A credit model asks about income, then about missed payments, and a leaf predicts default or not.
An online shop groups visitors by pages viewed without using any predefined segment names.
A grocer learns that baskets containing diapers also often contain baby wipes.
6.correctAnswer: An online shop groups visitors by pages viewed without using any predefined segment names.
6.explanation: No target label is supplied, so groups are formed from similarity alone.

6.question: Which situation illustrates Association rule?
options: A carrier splits 20000 subscribers into 4 groups by minutes, data use, and monthly bill.
A grocer learns that baskets containing diapers also often contain baby wipes.
A credit model asks about income, then about missed payments, and a leaf predicts default or not.
A team fits a churn model on 2022 accounts and scores it on 2023 accounts.
6.correctAnswer: A grocer learns that baskets containing diapers also often contain baby wipes.
6.explanation: The pattern links a condition itemset to a result itemset and is accepted only when support and confidence are high enough.

6.question: Which situation illustrates Decision tree?
options: A team fits a churn model on 2022 accounts and scores it on 2023 accounts.
A credit model asks about income, then about missed payments, and a leaf predicts default or not.
A carrier splits 20000 subscribers into 4 groups by minutes, data use, and monthly bill.
A deep tree labels every past student exam perfectly but misses many students in the next term.
6.correctAnswer: A credit model asks about income, then about missed payments, and a leaf predicts default or not.
6.explanation: Each internal test routes a record, and the leaf that is reached supplies the predicted class.

6.question: Which situation illustrates k-means?
options: A deep tree labels every past student exam perfectly but misses many students in the next term.
Of 50 diseased patients, 40 were flagged diseased and 10 were missed, and those counts sit in a class table.
A team fits a churn model on 2022 accounts and scores it on 2023 accounts.
A carrier splits 20000 subscribers into 4 groups by minutes, data use, and monthly bill.
6.correctAnswer: A carrier splits 20000 subscribers into 4 groups by minutes, data use, and monthly bill.
6.explanation: The algorithm alternates nearest-center assignment and center updates, and k is chosen before the run.

6.question: Which situation illustrates Model evaluation?
options: A deep tree labels every past student exam perfectly but misses many students in the next term.
A team fits a churn model on 2022 accounts and scores it on 2023 accounts.
Of 50 diseased patients, 40 were flagged diseased and 10 were missed, and those counts sit in a class table.
A gene study keeps 30 markers out of 20000 measurements before building a tumor classifier.
6.correctAnswer: A team fits a churn model on 2022 accounts and scores it on 2023 accounts.
6.explanation: Performance on unseen records estimates generalization, which is the point of evaluating a mined model.

6.question: Which situation illustrates Overfitting?
options: Of 50 diseased patients, 40 were flagged diseased and 10 were missed, and those counts sit in a class table.
A gene study keeps 30 markers out of 20000 measurements before building a tumor classifier.
A deep tree labels every past student exam perfectly but misses many students in the next term.
A 5-fold study trains on four fifths of the patients and rotates which fifth is held out.
6.correctAnswer: A deep tree labels every past student exam perfectly but misses many students in the next term.
6.explanation: The model has memorized sample quirks, so the training fit does not carry over to new data.

6.question: Which situation illustrates Confusion matrix?
options: A 5-fold study trains on four fifths of the patients and rotates which fifth is held out.
A filter raises 20 spam alerts and 15 of them are truly spam, so precision is 15 out of 20.
A gene study keeps 30 markers out of 20000 measurements before building a tumor classifier.
Of 50 diseased patients, 40 were flagged diseased and 10 were missed, and those counts sit in a class table.
6.correctAnswer: Of 50 diseased patients, 40 were flagged diseased and 10 were missed, and those counts sit in a class table.
6.explanation: Each cell records how often a particular true class received a particular predicted class.

6.question: Which situation illustrates Feature selection?
options: A filter raises 20 spam alerts and 15 of them are truly spam, so precision is 15 out of 20.
A gene study keeps 30 markers out of 20000 measurements before building a tumor classifier.
Among 40 real fraud cases, a detector flags 30, so recall is 30 out of 40.
A 5-fold study trains on four fifths of the patients and rotates which fifth is held out.
6.correctAnswer: A gene study keeps 30 markers out of 20000 measurements before building a tumor classifier.
6.explanation: Selection keeps some existing attributes and discards others rather than inventing new coordinates.

7.question: Which situation illustrates Cross-validation?
options: A filter raises 20 spam alerts and 15 of them are truly spam, so precision is 15 out of 20.
A search team reports one number that falls if either relevant hits or found relevant pages become scarce.
A 5-fold study trains on four fifths of the patients and rotates which fifth is held out.
Among 40 real fraud cases, a detector flags 30, so recall is 30 out of 40.
7.correctAnswer: A 5-fold study trains on four fifths of the patients and rotates which fifth is held out.
7.explanation: Each fold takes a turn as the test set, so every record is tested once and trained on the rest.

7.question: Which situation illustrates Precision?
options: A filter raises 20 spam alerts and 15 of them are truly spam, so precision is 15 out of 20.
In 1000 receipts, milk and bread occur together on 200 receipts.
A search team reports one number that falls if either relevant hits or found relevant pages become scarce.
Among 40 real fraud cases, a detector flags 30, so recall is 30 out of 40.
7.correctAnswer: A filter raises 20 spam alerts and 15 of them are truly spam, so precision is 15 out of 20.
7.explanation: Precision looks only at the predicted-positive set and asks how many of those predictions are right.

7.question: Which situation illustrates Recall?
options: In 1000 receipts, milk and bread occur together on 200 receipts.
Among 40 real fraud cases, a detector flags 30, so recall is 30 out of 40.
Among receipts that include cereal, 7 in 10 also include milk.
A search team reports one number that falls if either relevant hits or found relevant pages become scarce.
7.correctAnswer: Among 40 real fraud cases, a detector flags 30, so recall is 30 out of 40.
7.explanation: Recall uses the actual positives as the denominator and counts how many of them were caught.

7.question: Which situation illustrates F1 score?
options: Salsa appears with chips four times as often as salsa appears in a random receipt.
In 1000 receipts, milk and bread occur together on 200 receipts.
A search team reports one number that falls if either relevant hits or found relevant pages become scarce.
Among receipts that include cereal, 7 in 10 also include milk.
7.correctAnswer: A search team reports one number that falls if either relevant hits or found relevant pages become scarce.
7.explanation: The harmonic mean stays high only when both precision and recall are high, so neither error is ignored.

7.question: Which situation illustrates Support?
options: In 1000 receipts, milk and bread occur together on 200 receipts.
Salsa appears with chips four times as often as salsa appears in a random receipt.
A node split half yes and half no is more mixed than a node that is entirely yes.
Among receipts that include cereal, 7 in 10 also include milk.
7.correctAnswer: In 1000 receipts, milk and bread occur together on 200 receipts.
7.explanation: Support counts how often the itemset itself appears, divided by the number of transactions.

7.question: Which situation illustrates Confidence?
options: Among receipts that include cereal, 7 in 10 also include milk.
A node split half yes and half no is more mixed than a node that is entirely yes.
Salsa appears with chips four times as often as salsa appears in a random receipt.
Splitting customers on having a premium plan separates churners better than splitting them on shoe size.
7.correctAnswer: Among receipts that include cereal, 7 in 10 also include milk.
7.explanation: Confidence is a conditional share: it restricts attention to baskets that already contain the antecedent.

7.question: Which situation illustrates Lift?
options: A node split half yes and half no is more mixed than a node that is entirely yes.
Salsa appears with chips four times as often as salsa appears in a random receipt.
Splitting customers on having a premium plan separates churners better than splitting them on shoe size.
A spam filter multiplies per-word probabilities and treats words as independent once the spam label is known.
7.correctAnswer: Salsa appears with chips four times as often as salsa appears in a random receipt.
7.explanation: Lift divides the rule's confidence by the consequent's overall frequency, so 1 means no association beyond chance.

7.question: Which situation illustrates Entropy?
options: Splitting customers on having a premium plan separates churners better than splitting them on shoe size.
A spam filter multiplies per-word probabilities and treats words as independent once the spam label is known.
A node split half yes and half no is more mixed than a node that is entirely yes.
A lab model draws the widest street between two classes of tumor measurements in a plane.
7.correctAnswer: A node split half yes and half no is more mixed than a node that is entirely yes.
7.explanation: Entropy uses class proportions and reaches zero only when one class occupies the whole node.

7.question: Which situation illustrates Information gain?
options: Splitting customers on having a premium plan separates churners better than splitting them on shoe size.
A spam filter multiplies per-word probabilities and treats words as independent once the spam label is known.
A lab model draws the widest street between two classes of tumor measurements in a plane.
An unknown flower is labeled by the majority species among the three closest pressed samples.
7.correctAnswer: Splitting customers on having a premium plan separates churners better than splitting them on shoe size.
7.explanation: Gain subtracts the weighted child entropy from the parent entropy, so a useful split yields a positive drop.

7.question: Which situation illustrates Naive Bayes?
options: An unknown flower is labeled by the majority species among the three closest pressed samples.
A lab model draws the widest street between two classes of tumor measurements in a plane.
A biologist repeatedly merges the closest species groups until one tree covers all of the animals.
A spam filter multiplies per-word probabilities and treats words as independent once the spam label is known.
7.correctAnswer: A spam filter multiplies per-word probabilities and treats words as independent once the spam label is known.
7.explanation: Bayes' rule supplies the class probability, and the naive step factors the joint likelihood into per-feature terms.

8.question: Which situation illustrates Support vector machine?
options: A biologist repeatedly merges the closest species groups until one tree covers all of the animals.
An unknown flower is labeled by the majority species among the three closest pressed samples.
A lab model draws the widest street between two classes of tumor measurements in a plane.
A city map of crashes forms dense street clusters and leaves isolated rural crashes marked as noise.
8.correctAnswer: A lab model draws the widest street between two classes of tumor measurements in a plane.
8.explanation: The optimal boundary maximizes the gap to the nearest points of each class, which are the support vectors.

8.question: Which situation illustrates k-nearest neighbors?
options: A shopper near the middle of one segment and far from the next segment receives a score close to 1.
A biologist repeatedly merges the closest species groups until one tree covers all of the animals.
A city map of crashes forms dense street clusters and leaves isolated rural crashes marked as noise.
An unknown flower is labeled by the majority species among the three closest pressed samples.
8.correctAnswer: An unknown flower is labeled by the majority species among the three closest pressed samples.
8.explanation: The prediction is a vote of nearby labeled points, and no explicit boundary is stored during training.

8.question: Which situation illustrates Hierarchical clustering?
options: A shopper near the middle of one segment and far from the next segment receives a score close to 1.
A city map of crashes forms dense street clusters and leaves isolated rural crashes marked as noise.
Eight thousand labeled product reviews are used to fit a sentiment classifier.
A biologist repeatedly merges the closest species groups until one tree covers all of the animals.
8.correctAnswer: A biologist repeatedly merges the closest species groups until one tree covers all of the animals.
8.explanation: Each merge or split is kept, so the result is a hierarchy rather than one flat partition.

8.question: Which situation illustrates DBSCAN?
options: Two thousand labeled reviews that were never used in fitting provide the published accuracy.
A city map of crashes forms dense street clusters and leaves isolated rural crashes marked as noise.
Eight thousand labeled product reviews are used to fit a sentiment classifier.
A shopper near the middle of one segment and far from the next segment receives a score close to 1.
8.correctAnswer: A city map of crashes forms dense street clusters and leaves isolated rural crashes marked as noise.
8.explanation: Membership follows density reachability from core points, so arbitrary shapes and noise points are allowed.

8.question: Which situation illustrates Silhouette coefficient?
options: A shopper near the middle of one segment and far from the next segment receives a score close to 1.
Two thousand labeled reviews that were never used in fitting provide the published accuracy.
Eight thousand labeled product reviews are used to fit a sentiment classifier.
A class randomly assigns 70 percent of rows to training and 30 percent to testing one time.
8.correctAnswer: A shopper near the middle of one segment and far from the next segment receives a score close to 1.
8.explanation: The score compares a point's average distance inside its cluster with its average distance to the nearest other cluster.

8.question: Which situation illustrates Training set?
options: A class randomly assigns 70 percent of rows to training and 30 percent to testing one time.
Eight thousand labeled product reviews are used to fit a sentiment classifier.
Two thousand labeled reviews that were never used in fitting provide the published accuracy.
Ages from 0 to 100 are mapped onto 0 to 1 before a distance-based classifier runs.
8.correctAnswer: Eight thousand labeled product reviews are used to fit a sentiment classifier.
8.explanation: Fitting uses these records to set splits, weights, or probabilities before any final test.

8.question: Which situation illustrates Test set?
options: Household incomes are recentered and rescaled until the column has mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
Ages from 0 to 100 are mapped onto 0 to 1 before a distance-based classifier runs.
A class randomly assigns 70 percent of rows to training and 30 percent to testing one time.
Two thousand labeled reviews that were never used in fitting provide the published accuracy.
8.correctAnswer: Two thousand labeled reviews that were never used in fitting provide the published accuracy.
8.explanation: Because the model never fit these labels, their errors estimate generalization.

8.question: Which situation illustrates Holdout method?
options: A class randomly assigns 70 percent of rows to training and 30 percent to testing one time.
Blank salary cells in a hiring file are replaced with the median salary of that column.
Household incomes are recentered and rescaled until the column has mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
Ages from 0 to 100 are mapped onto 0 to 1 before a distance-based classifier runs.
8.correctAnswer: A class randomly assigns 70 percent of rows to training and 30 percent to testing one time.
8.explanation: Holdout performs one partition into train and test rather than rotating several folds.

8.question: Which situation illustrates Min-max normalization?
options: Ages from 0 to 100 are mapped onto 0 to 1 before a distance-based classifier runs.
Household incomes are recentered and rescaled until the column has mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
One invoice of 900000 dollars sits far above a column whose typical bill is near 40 dollars.
Blank salary cells in a hiring file are replaced with the median salary of that column.
8.correctAnswer: Ages from 0 to 100 are mapped onto 0 to 1 before a distance-based classifier runs.
8.explanation: The minimum maps to the low end of the range and the maximum maps to the high end, with values scaled linearly between them.

8.question: Which situation illustrates Z-score standardization?
options: Age is placed into child, teen, adult, and senior bins before association rules are mined.
One invoice of 900000 dollars sits far above a column whose typical bill is near 40 dollars.
Household incomes are recentered and rescaled until the column has mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
Blank salary cells in a hiring file are replaced with the median salary of that column.
8.correctAnswer: Household incomes are recentered and rescaled until the column has mean 0 and standard deviation 1.
8.explanation: Subtracting the mean centers the column at 0, and dividing by the standard deviation sets the spread to 1.

9.question: Which situation illustrates Missing value imputation?

Blank salary cells in a hiring file are replaced with the median salary of that column.

Age is placed into child, teen, adult, and senior bins before association rules are mined.

Face photos of 10000 pixels are represented with 50 components before clustering identities.
One invoice of 900000 dollars sits far above a column whose typical bill is near 40 dollars.
A color field with values red, green, and blue becomes three yes-or-no columns.

9.explanation: The record is extreme relative to the rest of the sample, so means, distances, or splits can be pulled toward it.

9.question: Which situation illustrates Discretization?
options: Age is placed into child, teen, adult, and senior bins before association rules are mined.
Face photos of 10000 pixels are represented with 50 components before clustering identities.
Answers to 40 correlated survey items are rotated into uncorrelated axes ordered by captured variance.
A color field with values red, green, and blue becomes three yes-or-no columns.
9.correctAnswer: Age is placed into child, teen, adult, and senior bins before association rules are mined.
9.explanation: Each numeric value is replaced by the interval that contains it, so the attribute becomes categorical and ordered.

9.question: Which situation illustrates One-hot encoding?
options: Answers to 40 correlated survey items are rotated into uncorrelated axes ordered by captured variance.
A classifier that always predicts the majority class misses the real pattern on both the fit data and later data.
Face photos of 10000 pixels are represented with 50 components before clustering identities.
A color field with values red, green, and blue becomes three yes-or-no columns.
9.correctAnswer: A color field with values red, green, and blue becomes three yes-or-no columns.
9.explanation: Each category gets its own column, so the coding does not invent a false numeric order among categories.

9.question: Which situation illustrates Dimensionality reduction?
options: A classifier that always predicts the majority class misses the real pattern on both the fit data and later data.

Answers to 40 correlated survey items are rotated into uncorrelated axes ordered by captured variance.
Face photos of 10000 pixels are represented with 50 components before clustering identities.
9.correctAnswer: Face photos of 10000 pixels are represented with 50 components before clustering identities.
9.explanation: The transformed records use fewer coordinates, but the kept coordinates are chosen to preserve variation or class structure.

9.question: Which situation illustrates Principal component analysis?

Answers to 40 correlated survey items are rotated into uncorrelated axes ordered by captured variance.
A very deep tree changes wildly when the training sample changes, while a one-level stump stays stable but crude.

Lowering an alert cutoff traces how the catch rate rises together with the false-alarm rate.
A classifier that always predicts the majority class misses the real pattern on both the fit data and later data.
9.correctAnswer: A classifier that always predicts the majority class misses the real pattern on both the fit data and later data.
9.explanation: The model class cannot represent the signal, so even the training error remains large.

options: A very deep tree changes wildly when the training sample changes, while a one-level stump stays stable but crude.
A biopsy that truly shows cancer is also marked cancer by the screening model.
Two churn models are compared by the area under their ROC curves rather than by one operating point.

9.question: Which situation illustrates ROC curve?

Lowering an alert cutoff traces how the catch rate rises together with the false-alarm rate.

A biopsy that truly shows cancer is also marked cancer by the screening model.

15.explanation: An impurity of zero for a pure node that uses class-share squares is Gini impurity.

15.question: A fully grown tree is perfect on training rows, so branches that hurt a validation set are removed. Which remedy is that?
options: Raising k to the sample size
Dropping minimum support to zero
Pruning
Deepening the tree
15.explanation: Cutting branches that do not help unseen rows is pruning.

15.question: A team averages the class probabilities of several different models instead of trusting one model. Which approach is that?
options: An ensemble
Single-feature selection
A majority-class baseline
Training to zero training error
15.explanation: Combining several models' predictions is an ensemble method.

15.question: Many trees are grown on bootstrap samples with a random subset of features at each split, and they vote. Which model is that?
options: A single unpruned tree
A random forest
Naive Bayes
DBSCAN
15.explanation: Bootstrap trees plus random feature subsets and a vote define a random forest.

15.question: A grocer wants product pairs that show up in the same receipt so the pairs can share an endcap. Which analysis is that?
options: Sentiment classification
Revenue forecasting
Market basket analysis
Store clustering
15.explanation: Finding products bought in the same receipt is market basket analysis.

15.question: Two rows share one student id, and a birth year of 3021 appears in the file. Which task addresses both problems?
options: Choosing k
Data cleaning
ROC analysis
Live scoring
15.explanation: Duplicate identifiers and impossible values are data errors, so the task is data cleaning.
